standard.title: Create geographical responses
standard.description: create descriptions, explanations and responses, using geographical knowledge and methods, concepts, terms and reference sources
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create descriptions, explanations and responses using geographical knowledge, methods, concepts and terms (AC9HG7S06). At Y8, responses must demonstrate more sophisticated use of geographical concepts and data representations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create descriptions, explanations and responses that connect audiences to geographical topics, use research findings and data representations, and demonstrate appropriate use of geographical knowledge, methods, concepts and terms.

nodes.label: Creating geographical descriptions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a description that connects the audience to a geographical topic using concepts and accurate information.
nodes.minimum_width: Students create a description of a geographical phenomenon that uses at least two geographical terms and provides accurate information.
nodes.typical_width: Students create a description that connects the audience to a geographical topic (e.g., the impact of a geological hazard, or urban slum conditions), using geographical concepts to frame the description and providing accurate, research-based information.
wider: Compare descriptions written for different audiences (expert, general public, decision-maker) and examine how audience affects language and concept use.
Investigate how geographers use precise terminology to communicate place-specific meaning that general language cannot.
Develop a description that integrates quantitative data with qualitative observation.
success_criteria: Creates a description of a geographical topic that uses at least two geographical terms accurately.
Includes accurate information that connects the audience to the topic.

nodes.label: Constructing geographical explanations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct an explanation that uses research findings to support ideas about the causes and effects of a geographical phenomenon or challenge.
nodes.minimum_width: Students construct an explanation using at least one piece of research evidence to support a geographical cause-and-effect claim.
nodes.typical_width: Students construct an explanation — e.g., the causes and effects of a geographical phenomenon such as urbanisation or geomorphological hazard — using research findings to support ideas and reinforcing knowledge of interconnections between people, places and the environment.
wider: Evaluate the strength of the evidence used in the explanation — is it sufficient, relevant and reliable?
Construct an explanation that addresses a counter-argument or alternative interpretation.
Examine how the choice of geographical concepts (interconnection, scale, change) shapes what the explanation emphasises.
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who describe without explaining — listing causes rather than making causal connections — cannot produce the explanatory responses required for S04 conclusions or K-strand demonstration of understanding. Evidence-supported explanation is the core output quality expected across the inquiry cycle.

response_modes.reason: The move from description to explanation requires a disciplinary scaffold: claim → evidence → geographical reason. Students need explicit instruction in how to use research findings as supporting evidence rather than background information.

success_criteria: Constructs an explanation that makes a geographical cause-and-effect claim.
Supports the explanation with at least one piece of research evidence.

nodes.label: Developing geographical responses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a response that uses representations of data and information to support actions and conclusions.
nodes.minimum_width: Students develop a response that includes at least one data representation to support a conclusion or action.
nodes.typical_width: Students develop a response using representations of data and information — e.g., a map showing the location of iconic landforms, a flow map showing international refugee movement — to support proposed actions and conclusions, demonstrating appropriate use of geographical knowledge, methods, concepts, terms and reference sources.
wider: Integrate multiple data representations (map, graph, diagram) into a coherent response.
Evaluate the effectiveness of different representation types for communicating the intended geographic message.
Develop a multimodal response that combines written, visual and cartographic elements.

response_modes.reason: Developing a full geographical response integrates description (Node 1), explanation (Node 2) and data representation into a coherent product that demonstrates the full range of geographical skills from the inquiry process.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multimodal response construction — combining maps, graphs, written analysis and reference sources — is a transferable geographic communication skill. Wider students can develop sophistication in selecting and integrating representation types to maximise geographic meaning.
success_criteria: Develops a response that integrates at least one data representation to support a conclusion or action.
Uses appropriate geographical terms, concepts and reference sources within the response.
